- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast window (e.g., 1–3 days) — adjust for lagged sentiment or event-driven volatility.
- When multiple auction events occur in 3–5 days, model fails to capture supply shock; reduce forecast by 1–4% for each event in 3-day window.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment peaks; align forecast slope with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
